purpose: Authoritative-vendor evidence delta adding CorityOne and Wolters Kluwer Enablon to the global manufacturing integration catalogue, and tightening Intelex integration evidence around authentication variants, custom-object discovery, pagination and throttling. CorityOne is spec-verified on its vendor-documented RESTful integration surface; Enablon remains discovery-queued on the existing vendor-thin connector scaffold because current public material confirms API-ready/SDK integration capability but not a stable outward protocol/authentication contract. No credentials, customer data, writes or private/plant-network surfaces were used.

patch.evidenceNote: Intelex's current developer documentation verifies a REST/JSON API over each customer's configured application model. V2 supports Basic and API-key authentication; the newer V6 secure API supports client-credentials bearer tokens when enabled. API requests preserve platform security settings for the effective user, but API-key and secure-token setup is limited to Admin/Full Access users, so authenticated evidence must prove the resulting technical identity is actually constrained to the approved records. The API is tenant/custom-object driven rather than a fixed EHS schema, caps sequential result pages at 500 records with @odata.nextLink paging, and documents a platform rate limit of 6 requests per second with 429/Retry-After semantics. WFM therefore reuses the existing REST adapter with customer-model discovery, explicit field/object allowlists, bounded paging and adaptive backoff; mutative object/user/task operations remain outside normal connector authority.

requiredPermissions: Intelex REST API enabled for the target tenant and required applications only
dedicated integration identity whose effective platform permissions are limited to the approved sites, applications, objects and records
prefer short-lived V6 bearer tokens where available; do not assume Admin/Full Access ability to create credentials means broad business-data access is acceptable
read-only access to the specific EHS/QMS/training/reference objects needed by WFM; no record creation, workflow action, task reassignment, user provisioning or archive/revoke authority
HTTPS with tenant hostname pinned; no arbitrary instance URLs or cross-host redirects
dataAvailableOrExpected: tenant-defined and standard application objects exposed through the Intelex Object Data API, including customer custom fields and relations
employees, users, groups and locations used to reconcile people/site context where the customer permits them
incident, hazard, inspection, audit, corrective-action, compliance and quality records where those applications are installed and exposed
training, competency or qualification evidence where implemented in the customer's application model
task/workflow references and responsible-person context where read access is approved, without taking workflow action
automationOpportunities: pre-shift readiness checks using approved training, qualification, safety and restriction signals without copying unnecessary sensitive incident or health records
identify sites, jobs or shifts with recurring EHS/quality risk and feed that evidence into staffing, supervision and training planning
reuse employee/location/group reference data to reduce implementation mapping and duplicate administration
use incident, corrective-action and task state to forecast temporary safety/compliance workload or specialist coverage needs
correlate skills mix, staffing level, overtime and shift outcomes with safety/quality events for executive and finance analysis
after separate write certification only, consider tightly scoped task/workflow hand-offs rather than generic object mutation
savingsHypotheses: reduce avoidable overtime and schedule churn by surfacing training, qualification and safety-readiness gaps before shift assignment
reduce duplicate EHS administration by reusing approved Intelex employee, location and compliance records instead of re-keying them
reduce incident/rework cost by correlating risk and quality outcomes with staffing, skill mix and shift conditions
shorten implementation by discovering the customer's existing application/object model and mapping custom fields once with versioned fingerprints
reduce API support effort through bounded 500-record paging, adaptive 6-request-per-second throttling and Retry-After-aware backoff
dataGaps: Intelex is configurable, so public documentation cannot establish which EHS/QMS/training objects or custom fields exist in a specific customer tenant
the platform is not normally authoritative for payroll, contractual hours, absence, agency commercials or production demand
API-key and secure-token setup is available only to Admin/Full Access users; effective least-privilege data scope must therefore be demonstrated rather than assumed
V2 and V6 authentication/API surfaces may coexist by tenant/version and must be discovered explicitly
health-sensitive or detailed incident narrative fields must not be ingested unless separately justified; WFM normally needs only a derived restriction/risk/eligibility signal
constraintsRisks: the documented platform API limit is 6 requests per second and 429 responses may include Retry-After; connectors must throttle and back off rather than retry aggressively
sequential result sets page after 500 records using @odata.nextLink; next-link hosts must remain pinned to the approved tenant and cannot bypass cross-host redirect policy
custom objects and fields create schema drift across tenants and environments, requiring schema fingerprints and versioned customer mappings
Object Data, User Management and workflow/task APIs can mutate business data and identities; WFM must allowlist read routes/verbs and keep those mutations disabled
tenant security is user-dependent; a successful token does not prove least privilege unless allowed applications, objects, records and fields are tested
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Keep Intelex at spec verification. Reuse the existing REST fabric; in an authorised sandbox/tenant, discover the exact API version and application/object model, prove the effective integration identity is least-privilege, exercise a bounded read-only page including @odata.nextLink handling, validate 6-rps throttling and Retry-After behaviour, fingerprint custom fields/relations, and normalise only approved worker/site/safety/qualification/restriction signals before promoting evidence.

systems.name: CorityOne
systems.evidenceNote: Cority's current technology vision explicitly documents open integration through RESTful APIs connecting CorityOne with enterprise systems. The CorityOne platform spans safety, health, environmental, quality, sustainability, learning and management-of-change workflows. Public material reviewed in this cycle does not publish the stable endpoint catalogue, authentication mechanism, scopes, pagination or rate-limit contract needed for authenticated WFM proof, so CorityOne remains spec-verified only. WFM reuses the existing REST adapter, keeps writes and Cortex AI/agent actions disabled, and treats occupational-health information as sensitive: normal WFM ingestion should use only customer-approved derived work-restriction/readiness signals rather than raw clinical records.

requiredPermissions: dedicated CorityOne integration identity limited to the approved tenant, sites, modules and read-only API surfaces
read access only to the minimum safety, training, quality, organisational and derived occupational-health fields required by the WFM use case
no incident/workflow mutation, management-of-change action, clinical note access, record deletion, configuration administration or Cortex AI agent authority
explicit customer approval and retention policy before ingesting any worker restriction/readiness signal derived from occupational-health data
dataAvailableOrExpected: sites, organisational references and worker identifiers used across the configured CorityOne environment where exposed through the tenant API
incidents, hazards, inspections, audits, risk/compliance and corrective-action context where licensed and API-exposed
learning assignments, training completion/performance and certification-related evidence from CorityOne Learning Management where licensed
quality and management-of-change context that can explain temporary production or staffing constraints where licensed
occupational-health surveillance/compliance and return-to-work status where licensed, reduced for WFM to the minimum approved restriction/readiness signal rather than clinical detail
automationOpportunities: pre-shift readiness checks that combine customer-mapped training/certification evidence with approved work-restriction signals before assignment
warn planners when an incident, hazard, management-of-change or compliance state creates a temporary staffing/skills constraint at a site or work area
identify recurring safety/quality hotspots and automatically recommend additional supervision, training or qualified coverage without changing CorityOne records
reuse governed site, worker and training structures during onboarding to reduce duplicate implementation administration
correlate overtime, staffing level and skills mix with safety, quality and training outcomes for executive reporting
after separate write certification only, consider narrowly scoped acknowledgement/task hand-offs; never inherit Cortex AI agent or generic workflow authority
savingsHypotheses: reduce last-minute overtime/agency substitution by finding training, certification and approved work-restriction gaps before a worker reaches the shift
reduce EHS/training administration by reusing governed CorityOne records rather than maintaining separate WFM copies
reduce incident, rework and disruption cost by incorporating current safety/quality constraints into staffing and supervision decisions
shorten implementation by reusing existing site, worker and learning structures where the customer API safely exposes them
improve workforce-risk reporting by linking paid labour and staffing decisions to safety/training outcomes without centralising raw clinical information
dataGaps: public Cority material confirms RESTful integration capability but does not publish the endpoint catalogue, authentication/scopes, pagination or rate-limit semantics needed for a tenant-ready adapter
CorityOne is not necessarily authoritative for payroll, contractual hours, production demand, machine state or agency-worker commercials
licensed modules and customer configuration determine which safety, learning, health, quality and sustainability objects actually exist

occupational-health records may contain highly sensitive clinical information that WFM neither needs nor should ingest; a separate customer-approved derivation must produce only the minimum restriction/readiness signal
training completion is evidence only and does not automatically establish legal work eligibility without customer-defined qualification rules
constraintsRisks: do not infer API authentication or token scope from Cority's marketing-level REST statement; discover and prove the actual tenant contract before authentication evidence
the platform can automate EHS workflows and now includes Cortex AI agents, but WFM normal integration authority must remain read-only with agent/action functions disabled
custom workflows, fields and modules can create schema drift between customers and regions, requiring fingerprints and versioned mappings
health/medical and incident data may be special-category/sensitive data subject to regional privacy, residency and retention requirements
multi-site enterprises require deterministic site/worker identity reconciliation before safety or training signals influence scheduling
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Keep CorityOne at spec verification. Reuse the existing REST adapter and global EHS data-minimisation rules. Obtain current customer/vendor API documentation or an authorised sandbox, identify the supported base URLs/API versions/authentication/scopes/pagination/rate limits, prove a dedicated read-only integration identity, enumerate only approved objects/fields, and first normalise site, safety, learning/qualification and derived worker-restriction signals before any evidence promotion.

systems.name: Wolters Kluwer Enablon Vision Platform
systems.evidenceNote: Wolters Kluwer currently describes Enablon Vision as an API-ready EHS/operational-risk platform and documents Enablon Hub as a self-service development kit for integration with third-party software, content providers, Edge/IoT devices, drones, beacons and wearables. Public material reviewed here does not define a stable outward REST/OData/SOAP endpoint contract, authentication/scopes, pagination or rate limits for a WFM client. WFM therefore reuses only the existing vendor-thin connector scaffold at discovery stage rather than inventing a protocol. The product's ability to connect to Edge/IoT sources does not grant WFM plant-network or device-control authority.

requiredPermissions: a vendor-supported read-only Enablon Hub/API/reporting identity once the customer-specific integration contract is obtained
site/module/object scope limited to the EHS, control-of-work and operational-risk records needed by WFM
no permit approval, control-of-work action, incident/workflow mutation, configuration administration or IoT/device-control authority
customer/site edge termination if the eventual supported interface reaches protected plant/IoT networks rather than a vendor-managed SaaS API
dataAvailableOrExpected: health and safety incidents, hazards, inspections, audits, actions and risk controls where licensed
process-safety, control-of-work, permit/isolation and operational-risk context where licensed
site, organisation, worker/contractor references and responsibility assignments where exposed
environmental/ESG and operational KPI context used by Enablon Open Insights where relevant to labour/operations analysis
IoT/edge observations already brought into the Enablon platform through supported integrations, without assuming direct WFM access to the originating device
automationOpportunities: incorporate permit/control-of-work and safety-risk state into labour readiness once a supported read interface is proven
identify areas requiring additional qualified supervision or temporary labour restrictions based on current operational-risk controls
reuse site, contractor and responsibility structures to reduce implementation mapping and compliance administration
join approved safety/operational-risk signals to absence, overtime, agency and production outcomes for forecasting and executive reporting
after separate write certification only, consider narrow task/acknowledgement hand-offs; never inherit generic permit, isolation or IoT control authority
savingsHypotheses: reduce staffing against temporarily unavailable/high-risk work by exposing current control-of-work and safety constraints to planning
reduce manual compliance administration by reusing approved Enablon site, contractor and action context
reduce disruption/overtime following safety events by bringing risk and control status into workforce contingency planning sooner
shorten implementation by reusing established enterprise/site structures once a supported read interface is obtained
dataGaps: public vendor material does not establish the outward API/SDK wire protocol, authentication model, scopes, endpoint/version contract, pagination or rate limits needed for a concrete WFM adapter
Enablon is not normally authoritative for payroll, payable time, contractual availability, detailed production orders or machine telemetry
actual available objects depend on licensed solution bundles and customer configuration
IoT/edge integration capability describes Enablon's ability to ingest data; it is not evidence that WFM may directly query or control those upstream devices
constraintsRisks: do not label Enablon REST/OData/SOAP or select a direct cloud endpoint until authoritative current technical documentation or an authorised tenant proves it
control-of-work and permit systems may contain safety-critical workflow authority; the WFM connector must remain read-only and informational
the eventual deployment can include SaaS plus edge/IoT integrations, so network topology must be discovered before deciding whether customer-edge termination is required
multi-site/global deployments require deterministic worker/site/contractor identity mapping and regional data-residency review
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Keep Enablon at discovery-queued on the existing vendor-thin scaffold. Obtain current Enablon Hub/API/SDK technical documentation or an authorised customer sandbox, identify the supported outward protocol, authentication/scopes, endpoint/version model, paging/throttling and read-only role; then reuse the matching protocol adapter instead of creating a bespoke stack, add any required customer-edge boundary, and only promote to spec verification when the interface contract is authoritative.
